note: Ground punch to the HEAD from side control, keyed against the pose it is thrown from. Lying across him his chest is flat: its forward points down at the mat and its up points along the mat towards his own head. The mount's clip cocks the hand 0.82 'up' in that frame, which from here is 82 cm out past his own head, and the arm orbited the shoulder to reach it. Keyed short instead, it still used the RIGHT hand - and in side control the right hand is the one at his far hip, 64 cm from the head, while the left is the crossface arm already resting 16 cm from it. Measured, that right-hand punch got 32 cm from the head and 27 cm from the chest: it finished nearer the body than the face it was scored against. It is the crossface arm that throws this: it slides off his head, turns over and drops back down into it from a hand's length. The elbow stays poled out to his own left, where side control already holds it.
